q: A nuclear reaction is a process in which a particle or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its ____.
e: A nuclear reaction is a process in which a particle or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its configuration. Gamma decay dumps excitation energy as a photon; Z and A stay put. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it.

q: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this ____ is released as energy according to Einstein's relation $E = mc^2$.
e: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is released as energy according to Einstein's relation E = mc^2. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Einstein is the name attached to this result.

q: A reaction where mass defect is released as energy is known as an ____ reaction.
e: A reaction where mass defect is released as energy is known as an exothermic reaction. Exothermic nuclear reactions lose mass; that mass defect leaves as energy. Defect is released as energy is known as an ____ reaction. exothermic.

q: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction is less than the total mass after reaction, external energy must be provided; this is known as an ____ reaction.
e: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction is less than the total mass after reaction, external energy must be provided; this is known as an endothermic reaction. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Endothermic nuclear reactions need extra energy because the products are heavier.

q: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of ____, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei.
e: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry.

q: If the neutrons emitted from a fission reaction go onto split other uranium-235 nuclei, the result is a ____.
e: If the neutrons emitted from a fission reaction go onto split other uranium-235 nuclei, the result is a chain reaction. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus.

q: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain ____.
e: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain critical mass. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei. Maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain ____. critical mass.

q: The energy released per atom in a nuclear reaction is about a ____ times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction.
e: The energy released per atom in a nuclear reaction is about a million times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction. million.

q: Nuclear reactor is a device in which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and ____.
e: Nuclear reactor is a device in which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and controlled. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei.

q: Fissionable nuclear fuel is the material for fission reaction to take place, such as uranium-235 or ____.
e: Fissionable nuclear fuel is the material for fission reaction to take place, such as uranium-235 or plutonium-239. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. For fission reaction to take place, such as uranium-235 or ____. plutonium-239.

q: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are ____ neutrons and need to be slowed down to maintain a chain reaction.
e: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are fast neutrons and need to be slowed down to maintain a chain reaction. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons.

q: ____ is a material to slow down fast neutrons released from a fission process, such as graphite and ordinary water ($H_2O$) or heavy water ($D_2O$).
e: Moderator is a material to slow down fast neutrons released from a fission process, such as graphite and ordinary water (H2O) or heavy water (D2O). A moderator slows fast fission neutrons so they are more likely to split U-235. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus.

q: ____ is to extract the heat produced by fission fragments when they slow down and stop in the reactor material.
e: Coolant is to extract the heat produced by fission fragments when they slow down and stop in the reactor material. Coolant carries fission-fragment heat out of the core before the metal melts. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered.

q: ____ are used to control the rate of reaction by raising or lowering them from the core.
e: Control rods are used to control the rate of reaction by raising or lowering them from the core. Control rods soak up neutrons; drop them in to quiet the pile, raise them to let it run. Of reaction by raising or lowering them from the core. Control rods.

q: Boron and ____ are neutron absorbing materials used as control rods.
e: Boron and cadmium are neutron absorbing materials used as control rods. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. Control rods soak up neutrons; drop them in to quiet the pile, raise them to let it run.

q: ____ is a protective barrier that reduces the passage of radiations from radioactive materials by absorbing them.
e: Shielding is a protective barrier that reduces the passage of radiations from radioactive materials by absorbing them. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. Dense shielding soaks up radiation so the outside dose stays low.

q: Materials which are radioactive and for which there is no further use are called ____.
e: Materials which are radioactive and for which there is no further use are called radioactive waste. Radioactive waste is leftover active material with no further use. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Many fission products are radioactive and dangerous, including ____, iodine-131 and plutonium-239.
e: Many fission products are radioactive and dangerous, including strontium-90, iodine-131 and plutonium-239. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma.

q: Strontium becomes concentrated in bones and iodine in the ____ gland.
e: Strontium becomes concentrated in bones and iodine in the thyroid gland. Strontium becomes concentrated in bones and iodine in the ____ gland. thyroid. A nearby word in place of thyroid would name a different quantity.

q: In an atomic bomb, an ____ chain reaction takes place so that an extremely large amount of energy is released in a short interval of time.
e: In an atomic bomb, an uncontrolled chain reaction takes place so that an extremely large amount of energy is released in a short interval of time. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei. Amount of energy is released in a short interval of time. uncontrolled.

q: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much ____ than those associated with coal, oil and gas.
e: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much smaller than those associated with coal, oil and gas. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. Are much ____ than those associated with coal, oil and gas. smaller.
